items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from George Kennan's "The Sources of Soviet Conduct" (the 'X Article'), published in Foreign Affairs, July 1947 — a article published anonymously in Foreign Affairs (July 1947), later declassified as authored by George F. Kennan available through the Avalon Project, Yale Law School:

"It is clear that the main element of any United States policy toward the Soviet Union must be that of a long-term, patient but firm and vigilant containment of Russian expansive tendencies... The Soviet pressure against the free institutions of the western world is something that can be contained by the adroit and vigilant application of counter-force at a series of constantly shifting geographical and political points."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of Cold War history (US.59–US.60), construct a CER (Claim, Evidence, Reasoning) response that analyzes how the ideological conflict between the United States and Soviet Union shaped the containment strategy outlined by Kennan. Your response should explain why containment was chosen over alternatives such as rollback or isolationism, and connect Kennan's logic to the specific conditions that produced the Cold War's ideological divide.
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento de "Las fuentes de la conducta soviética" (el artículo 'X') de George Kennan, publicado en Foreign Affairs, julio de 1947 — un documento de política del gobierno de EE. UU. disponible a través del Proyecto Avalon de la Escuela de Derecho de Yale:

"Es claro que el elemento principal de cualquier política de los Estados Unidos hacia la Unión Soviética debe ser el de una contención a largo plazo, paciente pero firme y vigilante, de las tendencias expansivas rusas... La presión soviética contra las instituciones libres del mundo occidental es algo que puede contenerse mediante la aplicación hábil y vigilante de la contra-fuerza en una serie de puntos geográficos y políticos en constante cambio."

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la historia de la Guerra Fría (US.59–US.60), construye una respuesta CER (Afirmación, Evidencia, Razonamiento) que analice cómo el conflicto ideológico entre los Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética dio forma a la estrategia de contención descrita por Kennan. Tu respuesta debe explicar por qué se eligió la contención sobre alternativas como el retroceso o el aislacionismo, y conectar la lógica de Kennan con las condiciones específicas que produjeron la división ideológica de la Guerra Fría.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — The United States adopted containment as its foundational Cold War strategy because Kennan's analysis identified Soviet expansionism as ideologically driven and long-term, making direct military confrontation unnecessary and isolationism dangerously naive. EVIDENCE — The student should cite: (1) Kennan's characterization of Soviet pressure as persistent and geopolitically mobile ('shifting geographical and political points'); (2) the post-WWII power vacuum in Europe that Soviet influence was filling; (3) the Truman Doctrine (March 1947) as the political expression of containment, committing U.S. support to Greece and Turkey; (4) the ideological incompatibility of Soviet communist totalitarianism with Western liberal democracy as articulated in the Iron Curtain's formation (Churchill's Fulton speech, 1946). REASONING — The student should reason that rollback risked direct war with a nuclear-capable adversary and that isolationism ignored the lesson of appeasement from WWII. Kennan's containment was calibrated to the ideological nature of the threat: since Soviet expansionism was driven by ideology rather than a fixed timetable, patient resistance at key pressure points would ultimately exhaust Soviet overextension. The response should connect the ideological origins of the Cold War (distrust forged at Yalta, Soviet refusal of Marshall Plan, installation of satellite governments in Eastern Europe) to the logic that military containment alone was insufficient — the contest was fundamentally one of political systems.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.59, US.60 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Presents a precise, arguable claim directly responsive to the prompt. Cites at least three specific pieces of historical evidence (e.g., Kennan's X Article logic, Truman Doctrine, Iron Curtain, Yalta breakdown). Reasoning explicitly connects ideological incompatibility to the choice of containment over rollback or isolationism. Accurately uses the CER framework with all three components clearly differentiated. Demonstrates understanding of the long-term, patient nature of containment as distinct from military aggression.
3 - Proficient: Presents a clear claim. Provides two pieces of specific evidence. Reasoning connects ideology to containment but may not fully explain why alternatives were rejected. CER structure is present but one component may be underdeveloped.
2 - Developing: Makes a general claim about containment. Provides one piece of specific evidence. Reasoning is present but superficial (e.g., 'the U.S. wanted to stop communism'). May conflate containment with other policies.
1 - Beginning: Attempts a claim but it is vague or inaccurate. Evidence is absent or purely descriptive without connection to the prompt. Little to no reasoning demonstrated.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Kennan's 'X Article' (1947); Truman Doctrine speech (March 1947); Churchill's 'Iron Curtain' speech (Fulton, MO, March 1946); Soviet satellite governments in Eastern Europe (1945–1948); Yalta Conference tensions (1945); NSC-68 (1950) as escalation of containment; distinction between Kennan's political containment and later militarized containment.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Presenta una afirmación precisa y argumentable directamente relacionada con el indicador. Cita al menos tres piezas de evidencia histórica específica (por ejemplo, la lógica del artículo X de Kennan, la Doctrina Truman, la Cortina de Hierro, el colapso de Yalta). El razonamiento conecta explícitamente la incompatibilidad ideológica con la elección de la contención sobre el retroceso o el aislacionismo. Usa con precisión el marco CER con los tres componentes claramente diferenciados.
3 - Competente: Presenta una afirmación clara. Proporciona dos piezas de evidencia específica. El razonamiento conecta la ideología con la contención, pero puede no explicar completamente por qué se rechazaron las alternativas.
2 - En desarrollo: Hace una afirmación general sobre la contención. Proporciona una pieza de evidencia específica. El razonamiento es superficial.
1 - Inicial: Intenta una afirmación pero es vaga o inexacta. La evidencia está ausente o es puramente descriptiva.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Artículo 'X' de Kennan (1947); discurso de la Doctrina Truman (marzo 1947); discurso de la 'Cortina de Hierro' de Churchill (1946); gobiernos satélite soviéticos en Europa del Este; tensiones de la Conferencia de Yalta (1945); NSC-68 (1950).
